name: PrimeTTS v2.1 Nano latency: 4 concurrent real-time requests, quality preserved

description: Baseline: 4 concurrent T81 requests on the Nano (resident GPU weights + per-stream arenas/streams), SNDR 70.08 dB

asi.hypothesis: establish the session baseline before any change
asi.noise_floor_note: N=4 wall measured 9917 ms and 10308 ms on two identical runs: ~4% run-to-run spread on the Nano; treat sub-4% deltas as noise
asi.phase_split: single stream T81: GPU kernels+sync 1673 ms, staging copies 39 ms, alloc/free 0; total run 4.44 s, so ~2.7 s is host graph work serialized against the GPU
asi.next_action_hint: attack the host side first (elementwise ops are scalar C; 4066 nodes; ~2.7 s of a 4.44 s stream)
asi.memory: free RAM dips to ~1119 MB with 4 streams at 32 MB arenas; guard is 60 MB so there is headroom

description: bin_op elementwise fast path (contiguous / scalar-broadcast fp32 ADD,SUB,MUL,DIV,MAX,MIN as plain vectorizable loops): ADD 349->108 ms, single stream 3863->3690 ms; N=4 wall unchanged within noise

asi.confidence: primary delta -0.7% is inside the ~4% Nano noise floor; kept because the op-level gain is measured (ADD 3.2x) and the change is a strict simplification with bit-exact output
asi.hypothesis: the interpreter's strided broadcast loop cannot be vectorized; give the contiguous and scalar-broadcast fp32 cases plain loops so gcc -O3 emits NEON on the A57
asi.next_action_hint: at N=4 the GPU is the shared bottleneck (conv kernels ~1.7 s serialized across streams). Attack conv kernel efficiency (cin split, threads, __ldg) and CUDA Graphs to remove ~180 launch+sync round trips per request. Remaining host items worth vectorizing: EINSUM 381 ms (2 calls), SLICE 207 ms, LEAKYRELU 200 ms
asi.result_detail: ADD 349.4->108.7 ms, MUL 99->63 ms; SNDR 70.08 dB and max|d| 2.247e-04 identical to baseline, so bit-exact as predicted
asi.why_n4_flat: at N=4 four streams contend for one GPU, so host-side savings show up in n1_stream_ms (-4.5%) and barely in n4_wall_ms

description: Share the host-side fp16->fp32 container conversions across contexts (ctab-keyed, refcounted, mutex-guarded): N=4 wall 10308->10072 ms (-2.3%, two runs), N=1 3690->3613 ms, free RAM +30 MB

asi.confidence: two runs 10070 and 10075 ms (0.05% spread) against baseline 10308: -2.3%, reproducible but modest; n1 3613/3668 vs 3690
asi.hypothesis: the 39 fp16 decoder records are 13.6M elements; each context converted them to its own 54.5 MB fp32 array, so four streams paid ~164 MB of duplicated host memory. Share the conversion across contexts (ctab-keyed, refcounted, mutex-guarded, container-path guarded)
asi.memory: min free RAM during N=4 on picard rose 1127 -> 1157 MB; the real relief is ~3x54 MB of host allocations removed, which matters most on pesi where N=4 measured only 66 MB free
asi.next_action_hint: host work is now ~1.1 s of a 3.6 s stream: EINSUM 377 ms in 2 calls is the single biggest non-GPU item, then SLICE 208 ms and LEAKYRELU 215 ms. At N=4 the wall is GPU-contention-bound (conv kernels ~1.7 s x 4 streams serialized), so the next big lever is GPU-side: CUDA Graphs per stream and conv kernel efficiency
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB and max|d| 2.247e-04 bit-identical to baseline on both paths; sharing is safe because the conversion is a pure function of the container bytes

description: Per-context capacity-sorted buffer pool for activation tensors: no latency gain (10087 vs 10070 ms), costs ~200 MB retained RAM at N=4

asi.confidence: 10087 vs 10070 ms at N=4 (+0.2%, inside noise) and n1 3604 vs 3613: no speed signal, while min free RAM fell 1154 -> 955 MB
asi.hypothesis: thousands of malloc/free pairs per request dominate host time; a capacity-sorted per-context buffer pool should remove allocator traffic
asi.next_action_hint: host side: EINSUM 377 ms in 2 calls (iSTFT basis), SLICE 212 ms, LEAKYRELU 135 ms are the remaining big items, and tv_alloc's full-buffer memset is unmeasured cost worth probing. GPU side: conv kernels 1.7 s per stream at ~80% of the measured 62 GF/s fp32 peak, so kernel tiling is a 1.2-1.3x lever at best; the 180 per-op stream syncs are ~7 ms, so CUDA Graphs is a launch-hygiene win, not the bottleneck
asi.rollback_reason: no measurable latency gain (N=4 +0.2%, N=1 -0.2%, both inside the ~4% Nano noise floor) while costing ~200 MB of retained memory at N=4 (min free 1154 -> 955 MB) from the 48 MB per-stream pool cap. glibc's allocator was already reusing the freed blocks, so allocation cost was not the bottleneck
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04, bit-identical to baseline: the pool itself was numerically clean

description: Specialized batched-matmul path for the iSTFT einsums (bkt,kn->bnt): EINSUM 377 ms -> below the 18 ms reporting floor; N=4 wall 10070 -> 9867 ms, N=1 3613 -> 3294 ms

asi.confidence: -2.0% on the primary against the previous best (10070 -> 9867) and -8.8% on n1 (3613 -> 3294 ms), well outside the noise on the single-stream number
asi.hypothesis: the two iSTFT einsums (`bkt,kn->bnt`, A=(4,9,3617) B=(9,16) O=(4,16,3617)) ran through the generic letter-space loop, which modulo-decodes every index per element: 377 ms for 231k FMAs. A specialized batched-matmul loop (innermost index contiguous in both A and the output, per-(b,n) double accumulator) removes the decode entirely.
asi.next_action_hint: host list is now LEAKYRELU 215 ms (35 calls, ~0.4 GB/s effective - suspiciously bandwidth-like, look at what else those nodes pay), SLICE 215 ms (214 calls), ADD 107, TANH 81 (libm per element), PAD 66. GPU: conv kernels 1682 ms of a 3.3 s stream.
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04 - bit-identical to baseline: same summation order (summed index ascending) and same double accumulator, only the index arithmetic changed
asi.pitfall_found: first attempt accumulated every n into one shared scratch row (outputs got the sum over all n): SNDR -39 dB, shapes all correct. The scratch must be N*T, one k-sum per (b,n) output row

description: Vectorizable fp32 fast path for LEAKYRELU/RELU/NEG/ABS in un_op: LEAKYRELU 215 -> 145 ms, N=1 3294 -> 3212 ms, N=4 wall unchanged (GPU-bound)

asi.confidence: primary metric flat (9867 -> 9865 ms, 0.02%, far inside noise); n1 improved 3294 -> 3212 ms (-2.5%) and the LEAKYRELU op time fell 215 -> 145 ms in the instrumented single-stream run
asi.hypothesis: LEAKYRELU was 215 ms of a 3.3 s stream in 35 calls because un_op evaluates every element through a double-precision switch (scalar, no NEON); a plain fp32 loop for LEAKYRELU/RELU/NEG/ABS vectorizes on the A57
asi.next_action_hint: at N=4 the wall is GPU-bound: host-side wins show up in n1_stream_ms and free CPU cycles, not in n4_wall_ms (this run proves it: -77 ms of host time moved the N=4 wall by 2 ms). To move the primary metric the next change must touch the GPU side (conv kernels 1.68 s per stream, kernel tiling/occupancy, fp16 activations to halve decoder traffic) or overlap host and GPU. Remaining host items: SLICE 223 ms (214 calls), ADD 116, TANH 82 (libm), PAD 73, SIGMOID 62
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04, bit-identical to baseline
asi.note: this path was in the discarded pool run (#4) and got reverted with it; re-applied cleanly on its own

description: Conv wrapper: bias resident in the ctab weight cache (no per-call cudaMalloc+copy) + async input staging copy on the stream: N=4 wall 9865 -> 9638 ms (-2.3%), N=1 3212 -> 3142 ms

asi.confidence: -2.3% on the primary (9865 -> 9638 ms) and -2.2% on n1 (3212 -> 3142 ms); SNDR bit-identical so no quality risk
asi.hypothesis: pt_v21_conv allocated and synchronously copied the bias tensor on every call (124 per stream) and used the blocking cudaMemcpy for the input staging copy. The bias is a container record, so it can be resident in the ctab weight cache like the weights (convT already did that), and the staging copy can be queued on the per-stream CUDA stream so it overlaps the previous kernel.
asi.next_action_hint: next GPU levers: (1) conv kernel efficiency - per-node profile shows dec/ups.0 ConvTranspose 195 ms, dec/ups.1 169 ms, and decoder resblock convs at 45-73 ms each (36 of them, ~1.7 s total); the kernel reads 12 KB of weights per thread from L2 and 768 strided x values, ~5x off the measured 62 GF/s fp32 peak, so a shared-memory tiled conv (cin chunks, x tile, W slice per block) is the big remaining lever; (2) host: SLICE 219 ms (214 calls), ADD 131, TANH 81 (libm per element), PAD 73. PT_V21_EKIND=2 now prints the top-20 per-node GPU times.
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04, bit-identical to baseline (weights, bias values and FMA order all unchanged)
asi.note: padding lanes of the output are never zeroed and never read by the host trim, so the async copy + resident bias introduce no uninitialized reads

description: Weight-staged conv kernel (cooperative shared-memory weight slice per block, input read coalesced from global): conv 2526 -> 1855 ms, N=4 wall 9638 -> 8787 ms (-8.8%), N=1 3142 -> 2807 ms

asi.confidence: -8.8% on the primary (9638 -> 8787 ms) and -10.7% on n1 (3142 -> 2807 ms), both far outside the ~4% noise floor; SNDR bit-identical
asi.hypothesis: the conv kernel gave each thread the whole (K x cin) weight row for its 4-channel group, so every thread in a 256-thread block re-read the same 12 KB weight slice from L2 (3 MB of L2 traffic per block) - ~5x off the measured 62 GF/s peak on the 36 decoder resblock convs. Staging that slice cooperatively into shared memory once per block (12 KB, fits 5 blocks per SM on the Nano's 64 KB) leaves the input reads straight from global, coalesced across threads, with no inner-loop __syncthreads.
asi.next_action_hint: conv kernels are now 1571 ms of a 2.8 s stream. Next: same weight-staging trick for the conv-transpose upsamplers (195+169 ms) and the big encoder convs (cin=768 -> 36 KB weight slice, needs cin chunking with double buffering, ~500 ms); matmul kernels are 50 calls at ~90 ms; host side SLICE 205 ms (214 calls) is now the top non-GPU item. A second lever: 2 blocks of 256 threads per SM means TT=128/threads=256 tuning is worth an A/B on the wsm kernel.
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04 - bit-identical to baseline: same k-outer/ci-inner summation order, same fp32 products, same padded output layout
asi.pitfall_found: an earlier full-tile variant (input tile + weight chunk staged cooperatively, 16 channels at a time, TT=128) was 2.7x SLOWER (6.9 s of conv): 48 __syncthreads per block per launch dominate on 2 SMs. Stage weights only, leave input reads global and coalesced

description: Weight-staged conv_transpose kernel (double-buffered shared phase slices): N=4 8787 -> 8207 ms (-6.6%) but parity gate FAILED (SNDR 54.24 dB T81, 6.47 dB T20) - discarded

asi.confidence: the speed signal is real (N=4 8787 -> 8207 ms, -6.6%; n1 2807 -> 2779 ms; convT host kind 359 -> 259 ms) but the kernel is numerically wrong, so the number cannot be kept
asi.hypothesis: conv_transpose threads each re-read their phase slice of the weights (ntap*cin float4) from L2, so staging the phase slices cooperatively into shared memory with double buffering should cut convT time the way conv weight-staging cut conv time
asi.next_action_hint: convT stays on the reference kernel for now. If retried, fix the staged traversal against a single-node byte-exact A/B (PT_V21_DUMP_T=<node>) before any benchmark: it is bit-identical on node 3821 (falls back) and 4019 (cin=1) and wrong on 3870, 4011, 4046 - so debug on node 4011 (cout=1, cin=16, K=16, s=4, 57920 outputs, 1507 of them differ). Remaining GPU levers: 12 encoder convs (cin=768, 36 KB weight slice - needs 2-lane groups) at ~42 ms each, 50 matmul calls (~30-170 ms). Host: SLICE 217 ms in 214 calls is the biggest non-GPU item.
asi.quality: parity gate FAILED: SNDR 54.24 dB on T81 GPU, 6.47 dB on T20 GPU (gate >= 60), max|d| 2.584e-03 vs 2.247e-04 baseline, deterministic across runs (not a race)
asi.pitfall_found: the deviation is deterministic and lands on a few percent of elements on exactly the nodes where the staged path is active - a logic mismatch in the staged phase/tap/channel traversal, not a shared-memory race. Two fixes were needed just to reach bit-identical on 3821/4019: a missing __syncthreads between a phase's compute and the next phase's staging, and seeding the accumulator with the bias (appending the bias at the end is not fp32-associative-safe)

description: Weight-staged conv_transpose kernel, barrier-safe (all threads reach both __syncthreads; predicate instead of continue): convT 359 -> 249 ms, N=4 8787 -> 8325 ms (-5.2%), N=1 2714 ms, bit-identical parity

asi.confidence: -5.2% on the primary against the kept best (8787 -> 8325 ms) and -3.3% on n1 (2807 -> 2714 ms); the same kernel scored 8207 ms when it was numerically wrong, so the speed signal is consistent
asi.hypothesis: convT threads re-read each phase's weight slice from L2 per thread; staging phase slices cooperatively into double-buffered shared memory cuts that traffic. The first attempt failed parity; the root cause was __syncthreads() inside divergent control flow (a `continue` skipped the per-phase barrier), which is undefined behaviour and corrupted a few percent of outputs deterministically. Rewriting the loop so every thread reaches both barriers unconditionally (predicate instead of continue) made it bit-identical.
asi.next_action_hint: convT host kind is now 249 ms (was 359). Remaining GPU: 12 encoder convs ~42 ms each (cin=768 -> 36 KB weight slice, needs 2-lane groups to fit shared), 50 matmul calls ~29 ms. Host: SLICE 205 ms in 214 calls, LEAKYRELU 139, ADD 105, TANH 81 (libm per element), PAD 76. Wall clock at N=4 is 8.33 s for 14.46 s of audio = 1.74x realtime; realtime needs ~6.0 s
asi.quality: bit-identical to baseline: T81 max|d| 2.247e-04 / 70.08 dB, T20 1.089e-04 / 69.67 dB, T40 69.94 dB, T120 67.92 dB, and byte-exact per-node dumps on nodes 3870, 4011, 4046 (the three that were wrong before)
asi.memory_watch: min free RAM sampled during the N=4 run dropped to 280 MB (1140 MB at the previous kept run). Shared memory is on-chip, so this is not the kernel's doing; the co-tenant LLM server (fwd35_serve) grows and shrinks over time. Worth re-checking on pesi (~767 MB headroom) and re-sampling picard before drawing a conclusion
asi.rule_learned: __syncthreads() must be reached by every thread of the block: any `continue`/`return` that can skip a barrier is UB on NVIDIA hardware and shows up as deterministic, sparse output corruption

description: Conv launch-shape heuristic (pick block size 32..256 from output length/block coverage): conv 1552 -> 1864 ms, N=4 8325 -> 9199 ms - discarded, keep threads=256

asi.confidence: 9199 ms vs 8325 ms kept best (+10.5%), and n1 3126 vs 2714 ms (+15%) - clearly worse, and the instrumented conv total rose from 1552 to 1864 ms
asi.hypothesis: conv blocks cover TT output columns x 4 output channels, so short outputs (flow encoder convs: len 81, cout 192, batch 4) leave two thirds of a 256-thread block idle. Choosing TT from {32,64,128,256} to maximize (block coverage) x (thread fill) should recover that. Only the grid changes, so results stay bit-identical.
asi.next_action_hint: keep threads=256 for conv. If short-output convs are attacked again, do it by splitting the *channel* dimension across more blocks (grid.y already = cout4/4 = 48 for cout=192, so the block count is fine) - the real cost at len~81 is that each thread runs the whole K x cin dot product, so the fix is more parallelism per output column (split cin across threads with a shared-memory reduction, which changes summation order and needs the per-node gate) or processing several output columns per thread with float4 loads.
asi.quality: SNDR 70.08 dB, max|d| 2.247e-04 - bit-identical to baseline (only the grid changed), so the discard is purely a latency verdict
asi.rollback_reason: the heuristic picked smaller blocks for the long decoder outputs too (Tout=3617 -> TT=128), which more than offset any gain on the short encoder convs: conv total 1552 -> 1864 ms, N=4 wall +10.5%

description: Conv kernel: 2-channel weight-staged variant for fat-slice convs (flow encoder, cin=768): conv 1800 -> 1520 ms, N=4 8325 -> 8168 ms (two runs), bit-identical parity

asi.confidence: two runs 8193 and 8144 ms against the kept best 8325 (both below it, -1.6%/-2.2%, spread 0.6%); the mechanism is directly visible in the instrumented profile: conv kernel total 1800 -> 1520 ms per stream
asi.hypothesis: the flow-encoder convs (cin=768, K=3, ~42 ms each x12) fall back to the unstaged kernel because their 4-channel weight slice is 36 KB, above the 16 KB shared gate. Halving the channel group to 2 output channels halves the slice to 18 KB (fits ~3 blocks per SM on the Nano's 64 KB) at the cost of twice the blocks; each lane reads its own component pair of the packed float4 weight, so every channel's accumulation chain is the reference chain.
asi.next_action_hint: conv is now 1519 ms of a 2.74 s stream, convT 249 ms. The same 2-channel trick applies to conv_transpose: dec/ups.0 (cin=512, ntap=4 -> 4-lane phase slice 32 KB, doubled for the buffer = 64 KB > the 32 KB gate) and dec/ups.1 (cin=256, 4-lane 16 KB doubled = 32 KB, currently at the gate limit) are the two biggest nodes (195 + 169 ms). Host: SLICE 206-216 ms in 214 calls is the top non-GPU item, then LEAKYRELU 139-151, ADD 110-118, PAD 71-84, TANH 81 (libm per element).
asi.quality: bit-identical: T81 max|d| 2.247e-04 / 70.08 dB, T20 1.089e-04 / 69.67 dB, T120 4.879e-04 / 67.92 dB, checks (T20+T81 GPU, T81 CPU) passed twice
asi.pitfall_found: CUDA treats two `extern __shared__` arrays of different element types with the same name in one translation unit as conflicting declarations ('declaration is incompatible with previous wsm') - name the dynamic shared array per kernel

description: convT 2-channel weight-staged variant (upsampler phase slices): convT 250 -> 578 ms, N=4 8168 -> 9599 ms - discarded, 2-channel trick is conv-specific (convT is input-traffic-bound)

asi.confidence: clear loss: N=4 9599 vs 8168 ms (+17.5%), n1 3079 vs 2710 ms, convT host kind 250 -> 578 ms. Parity stayed bit-identical (T81 2.247e-04, T20 1.089e-04, T120 4.879e-04), so this is a pure performance verdict
asi.hypothesis: the conv_transpose upsamplers (cin=512 and 256, 4 taps) have 4-channel phase slices of 32 KB and 16 KB, so double buffering pushes them past a workable shared footprint; halving to 2 output channels per block halves the slice, as it did for the fat-slice convs
asi.next_action_hint: convT stays on the 4-channel staged kernel (250 ms). conv is 1520 ms of a 2.74 s stream and is the main GPU target: the conv inner loop is ~1.75 instructions per FMA (one global x load + one shared w load + 4 FMAs per term). Register-blocking on the time axis - one thread computing 4 consecutive output columns and 4 channels (16 accumulators) - amortizes each shared weight load over 4 columns and should cut instructions per FMA to ~1.3. x traffic is unchanged by that change; W traffic (the reason the 2-channel conv variant won) is already minimal
asi.quality: bit-identical (T81 max|d| 2.247e-04 / 70.08 dB, T20 69.67 dB, T120 67.92 dB) - the 2-channel lane mapping is numerically exact, just not faster for convT
asi.rollback_reason: for conv_transpose the x (activation) traffic dominates, not weight traffic: halving the channel group doubles the number of blocks, and every block re-reads the whole input row set, so x traffic doubled and convT time went 250 -> 578 ms. The 2-channel trick works for conv (weight-bound) and fails for convT (input-bound) - gate them separately

Giving each thread four consecutive output columns (16 accumulators) amortizes each shared weight load over four columns and should bring it to ~1.4 instructions per FMA at unchanged traffic.

Remaining GPU idea with evidence: the 2-channel staged conv (already kept) for fat-slice convs. Host: SLICE 205-229 ms in 214 calls, then LEAKYRELU, ADD, PAD, TANH.

description: Fix device-memory leak in arena-overflow fallbacks (conv/convT/matmul now free what they cudaMalloc) + fuse LeakyReLU/scalar ops into conv epilogues: peak RSS 824 -> 739 MB, host LEAKYRELU 140 -> 58 ms; N=4 wall 8315 ms (flat)

Paired A/B on one binary (PT_V21_FUSE=0/1, two interleaved rounds) isolates the effect: LEAKYRELU node time 131/140 ms -> 58/62 ms, i.e. ~75 ms per stream of host work removed (about half the LeakyReLU nodes have a single consumer and fuse); CONV host time rises ~20 ms for the epilogue, so net ~55 ms of 2710 ms. At N=4 the wall is GPU-bound, so the metric did not move.
asi.hypothesis: memory accounting (PT_V21_MEM): 336 container records resident = 110 MiB (shared), host fp32 container conversions 84 MiB (shared, refcounted), per-stream host activation high-water only 10 MiB, per-stream device arena 32 MiB allocated with a **1 MiB high-water mark**, and ~123 MiB per stream of stray device allocations. Root cause of the strays: on arena overflow the conv/convT/matmul wrappers cudaMalloc'd a fallback and never freed it (the arena release only unwinds arena blocks), leaking device memory on every overflow - ~490 MB across 4 streams. Fixing the leak plus measuring peak RSS in measure.sh: peak RSS of the N=4 driver 824 MB -> 739 MB.

Also worth testing: the matmul wrapper should never leave the arena (its per-call buffers are ~1-2 MiB). Fusion for tensor x tensor Mul/Add (the 100 ms ADD / 60 ms MUL) needs the second operand device-resident, which is the device-residency project.

Also: a device allocation made on an arena-overflow path must be tracked and freed - the arena's release unwinds only arena blocks

description: Vectorizable fp32 exp/tanh/sigmoid for bulk tensors (degree-8 exp + Newton reciprocal): parity holds (SNDR 70.07 vs 70.08) but the wall does not move (8229 ms, n1 flat) - host transcendental time overlaps GPU work

asi.hypothesis: TANH/SIGMOID/EXP ran through the double-precision switch (a libm call per element, unvectorizable): 162 ms of host time. Vectorizable fp32 versions (degree-8 exp Taylor + Newton reciprocal + odd Taylor tanh near zero) measured as a paired A/B on the same binary, 3 interleaved rounds: total 2757/2683 ms (fast) vs 2695/2694 ms (libm) - no measurable single-stream gain, and N=4 wall 8229 vs 8193 best = noise.
asi.learned: GPU kernel+sync is 1457 ms of a 2.7 s stream and the conv kernels are 1520-1600 ms of it; that is the only thing that moves n4_wall_ms. The strided gather in the conv inner loop (xs[ci*ldx], 32 threads x stride) fetches ~8x more than it uses - packing the conv input in channel-contiguous float4 layout is the next lever.
asi.next_action_hint: pack the conv staging input so the kernel's inner load is one contiguous float4 per (k,ci) per thread (coalesced) instead of a strided gather; verify byte-exact per-node dumps before benchmarking
asi.pitfalls_found: four separate numeric landmines, each of which destroyed parity: (1) the Taylor coefficients for the natural-log Cody-Waite remainder must be 1/k! - the 2^r series coefficients are ln2^k/k!, and mixing them is off by e^r/2^r; (2) three Newton reciprocal steps leaves 2e-4 relative error, which this model turns into SNDR 10 dB - four steps are needed; (3) exp(2x)-1 near x=0 cancels away all significant digits (rel 3e-4 on tanh) - use the odd Taylor series for |x|<0.25; (4) 1/(1+exp(-x)) overflows to inf where the true sigmoid is ~1e-39 - branch to exp(x) for x<-87. Plus the gate: small EXP/TANH/SIGMOID tensors feed Floor/Cast/Gather, so an approximation applied to them changes integer shape arithmetic (T81 length 57856 -> 58880, SNDR -3 dB).
asi.quality_when_enabled: SNDR 70.07 / 69.66 / 69.94 / 67.91 / 67.46 dB on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29 (vs 70.08 / 69.67 / 69.94 / 67.92 / 67.46 with libm) and the same on the CPU path - the fast math is numerically fine, just not on the critical path
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric unchanged (8229 vs 8193 best, +0.4% = noise) and paired A/B showed no single-stream gain either; a neutral change with extra numerics risk does not belong in the tree

description: Channel-packed conv input layout with coalesced float4 inner loads: bit-exact (SNDR 70.08 on all cases) but conv kernel 14% slower and N=4 wall 9155 ms (+11.7%) - the read amplification was not the bottleneck

asi.hypothesis: the conv inner loop reads x[ci*ldx + t], so a warp touches 32 positions ldx apart (32 sectors fetched to use 128 bytes, ~8x read amplification on the dominant stream). Transposing the staging input into [time][channel-group] float4 groups on the host (blocked 2KB tile transpose) makes each warp read 512 contiguous bytes and use all of them, and each packed input feeds 16 FMAs (4 input channels x 4 lanes) with 5 loads - 1.31 instructions/FMA vs 1.5.
asi.key_numbers: paired A/B, 3 interleaved rounds: copy 137/149 ms (pack) vs 43/44 (flat), kernel+sync 1632/1633 vs 1428/1434, total 2956/2945 vs 2708/2692 ms; N=4 wall 9155 vs 8193 best
asi.learned: the conv kernels are not bandwidth-bound on this part: removing an 8x read amplification made them 14% SLOWER. What binds is issue/occupancy - 4 weight float4 loads per packed group keep 16 registers live per thread on a 2-SM Maxwell with a 12 KB shared slice, exactly the failure mode of the 16-accumulator experiment (#14, +39%). Traffic reduction is the wrong axis on this device; parallelism per output element and register pressure are the axes that matter.
asi.next_action_hint: kernel time (1520-1600 ms of a 1.43 s kernel+sync stream) is the only thing that moves n4_wall_ms; the traffic axis is exhausted, so target parallelism per output element (split cin across threads with a shared-memory reduction - changes summation order, gate on SNDR + per-node gate) and the per-op sync serialization (~1.75 s of cudaStreamSynchronize waits per stream at N=4) via device-resident conv->conv chaining
asi.pitfall_found: sizing the shared weight slice by packed *groups* (K*cin4) instead of packed *channels* (K*cin4*4) reads out of bounds: SNDR -0.02 dB and the output length changed 57856 -> 20736
asi.quality_when_enabled: bit-exact: SNDR 70.08 / 69.67 / 69.94 / 67.92 / 67.47 dB on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29 with identical max|d| - the layout and ordering math was right, the performance premise was not
asi.rollback_reason: packed conv kernel measured 1875 ms vs 1578 ms in matched A/B on the same binary (19% slower), and the host transpose added ~100 ms of copy time; N=4 wall 9155 vs 8193 best = +11.7%

description: Conv kernel with 2 output columns per thread (halving shared loads per FMA): bit-identical parity but conv 2407 vs 1580 ms in paired A/B - occupancy collapse again, N=4 wall 11676 ms

asi.hypothesis: the staged kernel issues one 128-bit shared load per (tap,channel) to feed four FMAs; at ~128 B/cycle of shared bandwidth the SM is saturated by that ratio. Covering two adjacent output columns per thread reuses each staged weight twice (shared loads per FMA: 0.25 -> 0.125) with 8 accumulators, keeping each column's accumulation chain in reference order (bit-exact, confirmed).
asi.key_numbers: paired A/B, 3 interleaved rounds: conv 2407/2448 ms (2 columns) vs 1561/1590 ms (1 column); kernel+sync 2253/2284 vs 1432/1440; N=4 wall 11676 vs 8193 best
asi.learned: this is the third register-blocking attempt on this kernel that loses (#13 convT 2-channel, #14 four columns/16 accumulators, now #19 two columns/8 accumulators). The Nano's binding resource is warps in flight on 2 SMs, and any per-thread state growth (accumulators, bounds checks, more live weights) costs more than the issue-ratio saving. The staged 4-lane single-column kernel at 256 threads is a local optimum; the traffic and ILP axes are exhausted. Remaining levers are structural: device-resident conv->conv chaining (removes the per-op D2H + host pad copy + H2D + stream sync from the critical path - measured ~1.75 s of cudaStreamSynchronize waits per stream at N=4) and stream-batched launches.
asi.next_action_hint: device-resident chaining: when a conv's output feeds only elementwise ops and then another conv, keep the output in the device arena, launch the next conv reading it directly with in-kernel zero padding, and defer the D2H copy and stream sync to the first node that actually needs the values on the host. Verify byte-exact with PT_V21_DUMP_T on the chained nodes before benchmarking.
asi.pitfall_found: in the 2-column kernel the tap offset k*dil was added twice (once via xs, once via the per-column offset), giving SNDR -0.79 dB with the output length intact - a value bug, not a shape bug
asi.quality_when_enabled: bit-identical to the reference on all five golden cases (70.08 / 69.67 / 69.94 / 67.92 / 67.47 dB, identical max|d|) - the numerics were never the issue
asi.rollback_reason: conv kernels 2407/2448 vs 1561/1590 ms in matched A/B (55% slower), N=4 wall 11676 vs 8193 (+42%) - occupancy collapse, the same failure mode as #14

description: Device-resident conv->conv chaining (no D2H/H2D/host pad/sync between chained convs, in-kernel zero padding): bit-exact, input copy 44 -> 27 ms, but N=4 wall flat (8375 vs 8193) and N=1 flat within noise - discarded, patch kept in .auto/chain_discard.patch

asi.hypothesis: keep conv results device-resident between chained convs: no D2H copy, no host padded copy, no H2D copy and no stream sync between two convs; each chained kernel applies the zero padding in-kernel.
asi.learned: the chain fires (input copy 44 -> 27 ms per stream), and the first version was 25-60% slower in the kernel because of a bounds test inside the channel loop; hoisting the test to the tap level made the kernel match the staged one. Parity is unchanged on all five golden cases. The net gain is ~17 ms of copy per stream, inside the Nano's noise. N=1 paired A/B (3 rounds): chain-on 2647/2664/3035 ms, chain-off 2669/2709/2730 ms.
asi.rollback_reason: neutral. N=4 wall 8375 vs 8193 best, N=1 flat within noise. The patch is saved in .auto/chain_discard.patch for a later attempt that also removes the per-op stream sync.
asi.retracted_claim: the earlier '~1.75 s of cudaStreamSynchronize waits per stream' figure was never measured. Do not rely on it.

description: CUDA sync policy = cudaDeviceScheduleYield (env PT_V21_SYNC, 0 spin / 1 blocking / 2 yield): N=4 7947 ms (best kept), paired A/B yield beats spin in 4/4 rounds, bit-exact

asi.hypothesis: With 4 streams on a 4-core A57, the driver's default spin-wait in cudaStreamSynchronize keeps every thread on its core while it waits for the GPU, taking cycles from the other streams' host graph work. Yield or blocking sync should give them back.
asi.evidence: paired A/B on the same binary, N=4 wall: yield 7699/7732/7990/7765 vs spin 8029/8004/8064/8080; blocking 8461/8044 (no better than spin; the wake-up latency costs as much as it frees). N=1 slowest stream: yield 2496/2502 (one 3304 outlier) vs spin 2786/2740/2718.
asi.quality: bit-exact: scheduling only, SNDR 70.08, checks passed
asi.next_action_hint: N=4 is now 7.95 s against 3.62 s of audio per stream. Next is the structural lever: batch the four streams per conv layer (grid.z = streams), or CUDA Graphs. Cheap follow-up: the remaining host work (SLICE 205 ms, TANH 81, PAD 64) now competes less with spinning threads, so re-check whether host wins move N=4.

description: glibc fp32 expf/tanhf for bulk EXP/TANH/SIGMOID (n>=4096): host SIGMOID 61->16 ms, TANH 81->62, EXP off the list (~80 ms/stream), parity holds, but N=4 7909 vs 7947 (-0.5%) and the paired A/B is flat - noise, discarded

asi.hypothesis: With yielding sync (#21), host work should compete less with spinning threads, so cutting ~80 ms/stream of transcendental host work might now show up at N=4.
asi.evidence: paired N=4 A/B on one binary: f32 7980/7765/7664 vs double 7776/7765/7728 ms; measure.sh 7909 vs 7947 kept. Parity: T81 70.08 (max|d| 2.237e-4), T20 69.69, T40 69.94, T120 67.91, sid1_T29 67.48, CPU path 70.08.
asi.learned: Even with yield, ~80 ms of host savings per stream does not move the N=4 wall. The per-stream critical path stays GPU-serialized at N=4. Host-only wins only matter for N=1 latency, and that metric is too noisy on picard to confirm them.
asi.next_action_hint: Stop chasing host micro-wins for the primary metric. Next: batch the four streams per conv layer (one launch with grid.z = streams x batch, shared weights), or CUDA Graphs per stream to cut ~180 launch+sync round trips. If N=1 latency becomes a goal, re-apply this change (a safe ~80 ms) and A/B it on pesi, the quieter box.

description: Uniform conv block-size sweep (PT_V21_CONV_THREADS 128/256/512, grid only, bit-exact): 256 is best (N=4 ~7.76 s vs 7.87 at 128 and 8.05 at 512, 2 paired rounds); default unchanged, so measure = 7954 ms = current state; sweep knob discarded

asi.hypothesis: Run #11 rejected a per-shape block-size heuristic, but a single uniform block size was never swept for conv.
asi.learned: 256 threads is the optimum for the staged conv kernel on sm_53 at these shapes. Block size is exhausted as a lever.
asi.next_action_hint: Remaining GPU levers are structural: batch the four streams per conv layer (one launch, grid.z = streams x batch, weights staged once per block for all streams), or CUDA Graphs per stream. Remeasure n1 too: this run's 2469 ms is the lowest seen, confirming that #21 yield also helps single-stream latency.

description: Raise the staged-conv shared-memory gate from 16 KB to 48 KB (sm_53 per-block max), so the K=11 and K=7 resblock convs get the weight-staged kernel: conv 1495 -> 1256 ms, N=4 7947 -> 6944 ms (-12.6%), N=1 2224 ms, bit-exact on all 5 cases

asi.hypothesis: The per-node profile showed the 65 ms decoder resblock convs (K=11 at cin=128, 22.5 KB; K=7/11 at cin=256, 28-45 KB) falling back to the unstaged kernel because the 16 KB gate was set for occupancy, not measured. The weight-staging win (#8) should apply to them up to sm_53's 48 KB per-block limit.
asi.evidence: paired N=4 on one binary (PT_V21_WSM_KB): 16 KB 7746/7783, 24 KB 7047/7065, 48 KB 6809/6797 ms. Parity is bit-identical on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29. Checks passed.
asi.generality: The gate is a byte limit on the weight slice (K*cin*16 B), independent of sequence length or case, and slices over 48 KB still fall back. No shape special-casing.
asi.learned: The occupancy argument behind the 16 KB gate was wrong for these convs. Removing per-thread L2 weight re-reads beats the loss of resident blocks per SM.
asi.next_action_hint: dec/ups.0 ConvTranspose is now the largest single node (~265 ms single-stream, cin=512, ntap=4). Its double-buffered phase slice is 64 KB, over the convT 32 KB gate, so it uses the unstaged kernel. Try a single-buffered 32 KB phase slice, or raise the convT gate toward 48 KB with a 2x24 KB buffer split across cin chunks.

description: convT staged kernel: single-buffer mode (one phase slice reloaded per phase behind a barrier) when the double buffer exceeds a 48 KB gate, so dec/ups.0 (cin=512, 32 KB/phase) leaves the unstaged kernel: convT 235 -> 188 ms, N=4 6944 -> 6697 ms (-3.6%), bit-exact on 5 cases

asi.hypothesis: dec/ups.0 ConvTranspose was the largest single node. Its double-buffered phase slice (2 x 32 KB) exceeded the 32 KB convT gate, so it ran unstaged. Each thread only uses one phase, so a single 32 KB slice reloaded per phase behind the existing barrier fits under 48 KB, with an unchanged arithmetic order.
asi.evidence: Single-stream, same binary: convT 234.7 ms (gate 31 KB = old behaviour) vs 188.4 ms (48 KB). Paired N=4: 6763/6561 vs 6750/6764. measure.sh 6697 vs 6944. Bit-identical on T81, T20, T40, T120, sid1_T29. Checks passed.
asi.noise_note: The N=4 delta (-3.6%) sits at the noise floor, but the component delta (convT -20%) is well outside it and the change is bit-exact, so it is kept. The barrier rule holds: every thread reaches both barriers unconditionally (the load is outside the live predicate).
asi.generality: The gate is a byte rule on the slice size; any convT whose single phase slice fits in 48 KB gets staged. No case- or length-specific logic.
asi.next_action_hint: GPU kernel+sync is now ~1.13 s per stream. Conv (1.25 s host-measured) dominates and is fully staged. Remaining: (1) cross-stream batching per conv layer; (2) the host ops at N=4 (SLICE 204 ms, PAD 74, TANH 81, SIGMOID 61) might matter more now that the GPU share has shrunk, so re-test #22 (fp32 expf/tanhf); (3) N=4 wall is 6.7 s vs 3.62 s of audio per stream, so 1.85x more is still needed for 4 real-time streams.

description: Retry of #22 (glibc fp32 expf/tanhf for bulk EXP/TANH/SIGMOID) after the GPU share shrank: N=4 6690 vs 6697 (flat), paired A/B within 1% both ways - still discarded

asi.changed_assumption: GPU kernel+sync per stream fell 1.37 -> 1.13 s (#24, #25), so the host share of the N=4 wall should be larger than when #22 was tested.
asi.evidence: paired N=4: f32 6715/6506/6538 vs double 6597/6562/6637 ms. measure.sh 6690 vs 6697. Host SIGMOID 61 -> 16 ms, TANH 81 -> 62 ms again; parity T81 70.08 (max|d| 2.237e-4).
asi.learned: ~80 ms/stream of host compute still does not move the N=4 wall. The four streams' host work runs in parallel on 4 cores and overlaps the other streams' GPU work, so per-stream host savings are hidden at N=4. The wall tracks the GPU's serialized total (~4 x 1.13 s = 4.5 s) plus the non-overlapped head and tail.
asi.next_action_hint: To move N=4, cut the GPU's summed busy time: cross-stream batching of conv layers (one launch over 4 streams, weights staged once per block), or more conv kernel efficiency. Host changes only for N=1 latency.
